question: What is the main job of anthelminthic medications?

options.A: To replace lost red blood cells
options.B: To lower elevated systemic blood pressure
options.C: To kill or expel parasitic worms

explanation: You've got this! Anthelminthics are simply the specific drugs we use to clear parasitic worm infections from the body. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why are worm infections so common in places with poor sanitation?

options.A: Parasitic eggs are easily spread through contaminated soil and water
options.B: Lack of refrigeration causes food to turn directly into parasites
options.C: Humid air causes human skin to produce worm larvae
options.D: Poor lighting weakens the human immune system against worms

explanation: Spot on! Worm eggs often pass through feces into soil and water supplies, which easily infect new people if hygiene is lacking. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which group of worms are flat, ribbon-like, and segmented?
explanation: Great try! Cestodes are our tapeworms—easily recognized by their flat, segmented ribbon-like bodies. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h2)

question: A patient has a roundworm infection. Which family of worms is responsible?
explanation: Well done! Roundworms belong to the nematode family, known for their smooth, cylindrical, unsegmented bodies. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h2)

question: How do benzimidazole drugs mainly attack parasitic worms?

options.A: By blocking cellular glucose uptake and depleting energy
options.B: By stimulating the human immune system to produce antibodies
options.C: By dissolving the outer skin of the host's stomach
options.D: By increasing red blood cell production in the bone marrow

explanation: Exactly! These drugs basically starve the worms by stopping them from absorbing the sugar they need for energy. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h3)

question: What happens when pyrantel pamoate affects a roundworm's nerves and muscles?
explanation: You got it! Pyrantel locks the worm's muscles in a tight paralysis so it loses its grip on the gut wall and gets pooped out. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why is it sometimes good if a deworming drug stays in the gut and isn't easily absorbed into the blood?

options.A: It ensures the drug travels directly to the brain tissues
options.B: It prevents the liver from metabolizing any medication
options.C: It reduces the need for patients to drink water
options.D: It keeps the medication concentration high inside the gut lumen

explanation: Makes sense, right? Keeping the drug right in the intestines means it hits the tummy-dwelling worms with full force! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which simple tip helps your body absorb oral albendazole much better?

options.A: Ingesting the medication with a fatty meal
options.B: Crushing the tablet and dissolving it in cold water
options.C: Avoiding all fluids for two hours after dosing
options.D: Taking the pill on an empty stomach with vinegar

explanation: That's correct! Taking albendazole with a bit of fat helps your body absorb it much more effectively. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which medication is the go-to choice for treating tapeworms and flukes?
explanation: Spot on! Praziquantel is our frontline medication for clearing out cestodes (tapeworms) and trematodes (flukes). [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h5)

question: A patient has both hookworms and roundworms at the same time. What kind of drug property do you need?

options.A: Strict specificity for a single parasite enzyme
options.B: Ability to cross the blood-brain barrier easily
options.C: Broad-spectrum activity against multiple nematode species
options.D: Rapid elimination through the renal system

explanation: You got it! Broad-spectrum drugs are fantastic because they tackle several different worm species in one go. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is a very common, mild side effect of most oral deworming drugs?
explanation: Totally normal! A little tummy upset or mild nausea can happen as the medication goes to work in the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h6)

question: What triggers the strong inflammatory flare-up called the Mazzotti reaction during parasite treatment?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the plastic pill capsule
options.B: Sudden dehydration caused by lack of drinking water
options.C: Direct toxic injury to human liver cells by the drug
options.D: The rapid release of proteins from dying microfilariae

explanation: You're doing great! When masses of tiny parasites die off all at once, releasing their proteins into the blood, it sparks a strong immune reaction. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h6)

question: When are most anthelminthic drugs strictly avoided due to risks to the baby?

options.A: During the final weeks of breastfeeding
options.B: During the first trimester of pregnancy
options.C: In patients over sixty-five years of age

explanation: Spot on! Since the baby's vital organs are forming during the first trimester, we generally avoid these drugs to keep the foetus safe. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why must nurses check a patient's liver function before starting a long course of albendazole?

options.A: Healthy liver function prevents worms from entering the bloodstream
options.B: Liver cells store the medication for up to six months
options.C: Hepatic enzymes are needed to activate the drug in the stomach
options.D: The medication is metabolized primarily through the liver

explanation: Brilliant! Because the liver breaks down these drugs, we need to make sure it's healthy enough to handle the workload without causing toxicity. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why do we usually need to treat everyone in a household if just one person has pinworms?

options.A: Healthy people absorb extra nutrition from the medication
options.B: Insurance companies require every family member to take pills
options.C: Pinworms spread easily among people living in close contact
options.D: The drug loses its potency if not shared by a group

explanation: You nailed it! Pinworm eggs pass around so easily on hands, sheets, and dust that everyone in the house will likely just pass it back and forth if not treated together. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h8)

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because they saw dead worms in the toilet after starting their deworming pills. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop taking the medication immediately
options.B: Advise the patient to take a double dose to kill remaining live worms
options.C: Reassure the patient that this is a normal expected result of the treatment
options.D: Tell the patient to report to the emergency room for a blood transfusion

explanation: Fantastic! Reassure them—seeing dead worms in the stool just means the medication is doing its exact job and clearing them out! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h8)
